# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura #1034 (KS-1215 revoked-session Bearer forward, T1 r1) @ `e4624218b`, pane `%97`, 2026-09-18 09:26:54 → 10:03 AEST, 36 min; scored by Wednesday at its verdict 00:02Z, spf/dkim/dmarc pass) | QA gate tier 1 round 1 (44 develop-forwarding routes, both modes, both prefixes) | 1 | 1.00 | 1.00 | **GO WITH FINDINGS**, no Blocker, no Major on a path #1034 changed. **Exceptional run.** Closed the class with real numbers (revoked-session forward 0 of 3,258 cells at head vs 558 at develop; register-connector forward 24→0, exactly those 24 cells changed, 0 status differences; planted controls firing). **Three things beyond the verdict earned the score:** (a) a READ that RAISED the pre-gate severity — `tenant-provisioning` re-forwards the inbound Authorization to security *for authz + audit*, so a revoked session had been authorising a key mint, not merely leaking a header; (b) it graded the reachable-vs-unreachable distinction honestly rather than inflating — the cache-get-throws HANG filed as a TICKET candidate, NOT a Blocker, because 72 adversarial + 9,774 census cells said nothing reaches it; (c) a **public self-correction**: its first reachability harness leaked a listener ~10 min because cleanup sat in the loop tail not the `finally` — caught by its own MID census, ended by verified pid, 0 listeners at close. Wrote `NOT-TESTED.written-first.md` BEFORE any run. Predicted merge tree `3f4dafb4f` over develop `f6669623c` and seat A's staged tree matched it exactly. 4 TICKET candidates surfaced (T-2, the no-timeout exchange fetch, is request-reachable and Major). |
| QA gate (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-491 tier 2 @ `08c6128`, run by seat S66, 2026-09-18 ~08:4x → 09:27 AEST; scored by Tuesday at its verdict 23:27:36Z, spf/dkim/dmarc pass) | QA gate tier 2 (three test-gap cells for the RD-465 banner: on-load tab, step-3 enforce, catch-path string) | 1 | 0.98 | 0.98 | **GO WITH FINDINGS, worst Minor — and the seat CHECKED ITS OWN GATE'S PROPOSED FIX AGAINST THE CODE BEFORE RECOMMENDING IT, and found it wrong.** The report said 'strip `active` from the fixture so the script must put it back'; the seat read the head, found `switchSection(` has one call site inside `openSectionFromHash()`, which returns early on an empty hash, so nothing re-applies it — the proposed fix would have produced a cell that fails for the wrong reason. Relaying a gate's remedy unread is a named coordinator failure; this seat did the check one seat earlier. Also: proved the new on-load cell is not a duplicate in BOTH directions (M1 red on the new cell with the four old cells green; M5 the exact inverse), proved the dead CONTROL end-to-end (whole 5064-line script replaced by a 78-byte comment: four siblings red, control green), stated its C-68 head-scope in the verdict itself, and flagged a counts trap that merge-tree cannot report. Recommended fix-before-merge over merge-and-ticket and wrote no code until ruled. |
| QA gate (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-490 round 2 of 2 @ `23efec8`, run by seat S66, 2026-09-18 ~07:0x → 08:36 AEST; scored by Tuesday at its verdict 22:36:35Z, spf/dkim/dmarc pass) | QA gate tier 1 round 2 (real-browser guard for the open-site banner: 9 must-measures, 11 guard mutations, 8 round-1 concealments) | 1 | 0.97 | 0.97 | **GO, worst Low, cap not engaged. Every headline number re-derived by the seat from the evidence rather than relayed: the forced port-collision refusal quoted from the mutation json, the Linux INK lows parsed per page (min 0.116 vs the 0.10 bar), the verify line found twice.** All 8 round-1 green concealments now r

> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)

> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."
